messages:
Maya: Heads up — we need a new GPU nodepool in us-midwest1 for bursty LLM inference traffic. Goal: tiny baseline (2 x a10g) + burst to ~20 nodes (mix of preemptible a10g + a100 on-demand). Quota blocked rn, but want design feedback before I open tickets.

Alvin: Do we want a single heterogeneous pool or two pools (baseline a10g, burst a100)? cost/packing tradeoffs.

Maya: Leaning toward one pool with mixed instance types to keep scheduling simpler and let CA binpack. Taints to keep non-gpu workloads off. Will set nodeSelector/affinity for small models to prefer a10g.

Raj: CA tuning is key. What min/max, and scale-down behaviour? We should avoid thrash during sudden bursts.

Maya: Proposed CA values:
```yaml
nodePool: gpu-midwest-burst
minSize: 2
maxSize: 20
autoscaling:
  scaleDownUnneededTime: 10m
  scaleDownUtilizationThreshold: 0.25
  balanceSimilarNodeGroups: true
```
Keep scaleDownUnneededTime at 10m to avoid immediate churn; use lower utilization threshold so CA keeps nodes around during short tails.

Sophie: Make sure model-serving pods have a high priorityClass so they preempt less-critical batch pods. Also add PodDisruptionBudget for replicas.

Maya: Agreed. Example priority + taint config:
```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: system-llm-serving
value: 100000
globalDefault: false
description: High priority for real-time inference pods
---
# nodepool taint created on nodes
key: gpu
value: reserved
effect: NoSchedule
```
Pods get toleration + priorityClassName: `system-llm-serving`.

Leon: Watch eviction behavior — preemptible a10gs are fine, but if we mix on-demand a100s with preemptible a10gs CA might shrink a10g first causing model placement shifts. We should set `scaleDownUnneededTime` longer for a100s or use `priority`/`descheduler` hints.

Maya: Good point. Another option: label node pool sub-classes and set `node-affinity` on critical pods to prefer a100 when needed, and use `podTopologySpread` to avoid hot-spot packing.

Alvin: Cost question: a100s for cold-starts are expensive. Can we fall back to CPU-only pool for small requests when GPUs unavailable? Might be slower but keeps service up.

Maya: Yes we should register a fallback route in the router policy: prefer gpu pool, failover to cpu-infer pool with a timeout (200ms) and degrade gracefully.

Raj: What about quotas? I can help with ticket. We need per-region vCPU/GPU and accelerators.

ops-bot: Quota ticket created: Q-3421 (requesting 25 GPUs in us-midwest1). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/Q-3421 :white_check_mark:

Maya: Thanks @Raj and @ops-bot. I'll also open infra PR with CA config + taints + new priority class.

deploy-bot: k8s: nodepool creation job queued for gpu-midwest-burst (pending quota).

Sophie: Also add e2e for scheduler behaviour (simulate scale-up with 50 concurrent requests) and an alert if pod scheduling latency > 5s for >2m.

Maya: Yup adding tests + alert. Action items:
- Maya: open PR with YAML + CA tuning + router fallback (today)
- Raj: escalate quota Q-3421 if no response in 24h
- Leon: draft a short runbook for eviction behavior and manual pinning to a100s
- Sophie: add e2e and alert (this sprint)

Maya: Any other blockers? :eyes:

Alvin: One last nit — set node auto-repair off for burst nodes while scale activity is high (to avoid replacement churn).

Maya: Good call, will set `autoRepair: false` for the burst pool until we verify stability.

Leon: thumbs up.

Maya: I'll post the PR link here once done. Thanks all. :rocket:
